prior_result.explanation: The current meta description is still the original wording without the recognition-log sentence, so the 2026-10 change was never applied and the hypothesis was not actually tested; incidentally, Claude and ChatGPT both described the recognition log in 2026-11 without it being in the meta description, which points to the body and FAQ as the source of their summaries.

proposal.observation: All three models are familiar on search_results for the second consecutive month and describe the project accurately; Claude and ChatGPT both name the self-recognition log, while Gemini describes the board, daily answers, themes and open data but omits the recognition log entirely. Claude also flags confusion with an unrelated Polish company of a similar name.
proposal.hypothesis: Gemini's summary is built mainly from the title and meta description rather than the full FAQ body: if the recognition log is named in the meta description, Gemini should mention it in the 2026-12 log; if Gemini still omits it while Claude and ChatGPT continue to cite it, the meta description is not the lever for Gemini and the omission is a depth-of-crawl issue in the body instead.

change.current_text: Each month, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini name the hardest unsolved problems in marketing technology. Each day, all three explain how they would attack one of them, in the same format, side by side. Open data, open harness.
change.proposed_text: Each month, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini name the hardest unsolved problems in marketing technology. Each day, all three explain how they would attack one of them, in the same format, side by side. A public recognition log records what those same models say this site is. Open data, open harness.
change.rationale: This is the 2026-10 proposal, which was never applied, so the test is still open, and it now has a sharper single-model prediction: Gemini is the only model that does not mention the recognition log.

proposal.expected_signal: In 2026-12, Gemini's verbatim answer names the recognition log or the self-recognition experiment, while Claude and ChatGPT keep doing so; a Gemini answer that still omits it falsifies the meta-description hypothesis and points the next experiment at the body and navigation.
